subject.title: [Bug] web_fetch fails in dual-stack networks when DNS returns IPv6 special-use addresses

question: Should OpenClaw relax the default SSRF DNS-answer rule so mixed result sets can proceed after dropping blocked candidates, or keep the current any-blocked-answer fail-closed rule?
rationale: The implementation is narrow, but allowing one safe DNS answer to carry the request changes the default outbound fetch SSRF boundary and should reflect maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
options.body: Allow requests only when at least one resolved address is allowed, pass only allowed addresses into the pinned dispatcher, and test mixed-answer plus all-blocked cases.

options.title: Keep any-blocked fail-closed
options.body: Treat the current behavior as intentional strict SSRF protection and document trusted proxy or fake-IP opt-in paths for affected networks.

options.title: Make polluted DNS handling opt-in
options.body: Preserve the current default and add or reuse an operator-controlled SSRF policy knob for mixed polluted DNS environments.

recommendation.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
recommendation.body: Allow requests only when at least one resolved address is allowed, pass only allowed addresses into the pinned dispatcher, and test mixed-answer plus all-blocked cases.

likelyOwner.reason: The security-boundary history and repeated SSRF maintenance point to steipete as the best available owner for default DNS-answer semantics.
